decisions.reason: The candidate's same-message introduction already captures J_BTN3, J_BTN4, and J_SW; the source modification concerns the separate reset connection and on-board BOOT control.
The BOOT-button placement and reset wiring do not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or its breakout requirement.
The reset connection uses EN to GND and no BOOT GPIO assignment is specified, so the source modification does not change the candidate's GPIO compatibility state.
The reset and BOOT-control decisions do not alter I2C pull-ups, series resistance, placement, speed, or cable assumptions.
J_RESET wiring refers to the ESP32 EN reset signal, not the MT3608 boost-converter EN signal controlling the 5V rail.
J_RESET is a panel reset connection, and the source does not modify either power-to-main interboard connector or its pinout.
Keeping BOOT on-board for development does not change the USB-C programming interface or establish a change to native USB behavior.
The source modification does not change the INA219, measured rails, or power-telemetry behavior.
The BOOT and reset-control details do not alter the standalone regulator, source selection, activation condition, or powered load.
The circuit decision does not change the candidate's general BOM obligations or its recorded R6 attributes; propagating component details would require separate BOM evidence.
The source modification does not affect LED supply voltage or data-level shifting.
The BOOT and reset controls belong to the main-board design and do not change the power board's mechanical layout.
